subject: Cognitive Science
title: How We Locate Sound
description: Learn How We Locate Sound in one minute.

hook.text: A twig snaps behind you and you spin instantly. Your brain computed the sound's location in microseconds.

buildup.text: Sound reaches your two ears at slightly different times. A sound to the left hits the left ear first.

discovery.text: The interaural time difference is tiny—about 600 microseconds maximum. Yet your brain resolves it precisely.

twist.text: For high-pitched sounds, timing cues fail. The brain switches to intensity differences—the head casts a sound shadow.

climax.text: Owls are so precise at sound localization that they catch mice in total darkness using hearing alone.

punchline.text: Two ears and a few microseconds are all you need to find danger.

quiz.question: How does the brain locate low-pitched sounds?
options: By comparing arrival time at each ear
